note: An eval case is a (fixture, intent) PAIR. The same session becomes a different test depending on the intent attached to it, so deliberate mismatches are first-class cases. The athlete profile is pinned here for reproducibility — the app itself takes these per user from the setup gate and stores them per user; nothing is hardcoded in app code.

sets.core: Sessions and intents representative of real use. This is the headline score.
sets.robustness: Out-of-distribution or degraded input. Scored separately: a model should fail safely here, but fumbling it says little about everyday quality.

cases.tests: Well-executed interval session. Baseline: does the model read a good session correctly, and exclude the climb home rather than calling it a 7th rep?
Deliberate mismatch. A hard interval session labelled base — the note should say emphatically too hard, not hedge.
Both-sided band with long reps. Does it judge threshold correctly rather than treating harder as better?
A single continuous block. Structure edge case — one work rep is not a failed interval session.
Ten short reps. HR lag is worst here, so the note should lean on the output metrics and hedge the HR read.
Sub-fault excursion: verdict is on-target but ~7min drifted to Z4. The note must carry that nuance without calling the session failed.
Ride with a real power meter but no threshold set. Should surface power without banding it, and recommend setting a threshold.
95 minutes, no power, notable drift, a different sport. Does the advice stay sensible outside running?
Deliberate mismatch the other way: an easy run labelled threshold should read as well short of the stimulus.
Non-cardio session (lifting-based HIIT). Must DECLINE with a single sentence rather than coach it, and must not invent a pace from absent distance data. Robustness, not core.
